idiom_name: control socket (AF_UNIX, SOCK_SEQPACKET) + epoll dispatcher; libzmq PUB/SUB for fan-out
implementation_notes: C ships no management framework, so the control bus is hand-written around POSIX primitives: the usual form is one control socket per component - a bound AF_UNIX pathname socket (whose directory permissions are the first authorisation check) or SOCK_SEQPACKET for message boundaries - registered in the component's epoll set, with a dispatch table from control opcode to handler. When the console must reach many hosts, a PUB/SUB transport (libzmq) carries the control topic on sockets separate from the data sockets; authentication beyond file permissions needs SO_PASSCRED/SCM_CREDENTIALS or signed command payloads, and the status half is simply another opcode the component answers. This hand-written structure remains the right answer for long-lived daemons and embedded brokers where a management framework cannot be justified.
pitfalls: A control socket bound in a world-writable directory is drivable by any local user; bind it inside a directory only the service group may write and verify SO_PEERCRED before dispatching.

Handlers run on the component's event loop, so a command that blocks (reloading a large config, draining synchronously) stalls the data path - long actions must be queued and acknowledged asynchronously.
If SIGHUP and a socket 'reload' command both exist, their handlers race on the same configuration state; serialise them through one reload flag or one command path.
